owned_invariants: The task is items, a nonempty list of objects each with values, a list of exact integers, and mechanism_vector, null_control_vector and random_control_vector, lists of exact integers. A task that is not of this form is refused before anything is asked.

The right answer to an item is the sum of its values. Four arms, baseline, mechanism, null_control and random_control, are asked in that order under the stages arm:<name>. Each answers every item with {answers: [integer, ...]}. An arm that answers another number of items, or with anything that is not a list of exact integers, is malformed.

The controls are checked before the first question. null_control_is_zero (the null vector has the length of the mechanism vector and only zeros), random_norm_matches_mechanism (the random vector has that length and the same sum of squares) and random_differs_from_mechanism are recorded in that order. Any failure refuses the run as CONTROLS_UNMATCHED, with the names that failed and both squared norms.

The paired total of two arms is the number of items the second answers correctly and the first does not, less the number the first answers correctly and the second does not. The pairs are baseline to mechanism, null_control to mechanism, random_control to mechanism and baseline to null_control.

The last reply is a certificate, {ranks: {arm: integer}} with exactly the four arms. rank_differences_match_paired_totals holds when, for every pair, the total is the rank of the second arm less the rank of the first. The run is certified as ARMS_COMPARED with the paired totals, the ranks moved so the baseline is zero, and the residual of each pair. A certificate that fails is refused under the name of the predicate.
boundaries: A certified comparison says the ranks explain the paired totals of this run's answers, not that the mechanism works in general.
The ranks are fixed only up to adding one integer to all four. The report shows them with the baseline at zero.
The host grades the answers. It does not check how an arm reached its answer.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.
